rows.title: `agent` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: An agent: a model with tools and a system prompt, with memory per thread.
body: An **agent**: a model with tools and a system prompt, with memory per thread.

A model with tools and a system prompt, with memory per thread. Its tools are the `tools` it receives; `model` names the chat model connection. `~guide.ask(text, thread = "user-1")` answers; `stream(text)` gives the answer piece by piece.
prompt: string = "You answer questions about the characters. Use the tools."
Its file: `components/{component}/ai/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).

rows.title: `appConfig` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: The configuration of the app: its connections (databases, Redis, Kafka, models, vectors).
body: The **configuration of the app**: its connections (databases, Redis, Kafka, models, vectors).

The connections of the app (`appConfig`, `config/project_config.nuc`) and of a component (`config`): opened at start and closed at stop. Databases: `Postgres`, `MySQL`, `SQLite` (`url` picks the async driver, `createTables = true` creates the tables); `Redis`; `Kafka(servers, group)`; models: `OpenAI(model)`, `Ollama(model, baseUrl)`, `Embeddings(model)`; `Chroma(collection, embeddings, path)`. Each has a `name` (default `"default"`). `env("VAR", "default")` reads the environment.
Its file: `config/project_config.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).

rows.title: `controller` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: REST routes of the API.
body: REST routes: `@controller("path")` and `@get`, `@post` (201), `@put`, `@patch`, `@delete` with the route (`"{id}"`: a path parameter; segments without a leading slash). A parameter that is a model is the JSON body; an entity is read and answered as its fields. A `Result` answers its value, or the error's status and message.
Its file: `components/{component}/api/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).
The smallest file of the kind (what `dragonfly make controller books Book` writes):

rows.title: `entity` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: A table of the project's database.
body: A table. In `components/<c>/data/entities/` the kind is given by the folder; elsewhere write `entity`. `@entity("table")` names the table (default: the name in snake_case). Each field is a column: `@primary(generated = true)` (a key the database gives), `@primary()` (a key the app gives), `@column(length = 100, unique = true, index = true, nullable = true, name = "x")`, `@created()`, `@updated()`; without a decorator it is a column too. Relations: `@manyToOne` (+ its column `<name>Id`), `@oneToMany`, `@manyToMany` + `@joinTable`, `@oneToOne` + `@joinColumn`; a relation field is optional and loaded only by `relations(...)` (N0308). Its SQL type comes from the field type; `name?: T` is nullable; a default goes to the column.
Its file: `components/{component}/data/entities/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).
The smallest file of the kind (what `dragonfly make entity books Book` writes):

rows.title: `graph` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: A graph of steps: its methods are the nodes.
body: A **graph** of steps: its methods are the nodes.

A graph of steps: `state` is its state (`messages: Messages` keeps a conversation). Each method of the `graph` is a node that receives the state and returns what changes; `@start` marks the first one and `@next("node")` the one after it (`"end"` ends). A node can also return `Command(goto = "node", update = {...})` to choose at run time. `~review.run(state, thread)` runs it.
Its file: `components/{component}/ai/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).

rows.title: `listener` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: A Kafka consumer: `@consumer("topic")` methods receive the messages.
body: A **Kafka consumer**: `@consumer("topic")` methods receive the messages.

A Kafka consumer: each `@consumer("topic")` method receives the messages of the topic, parsed as the type of its parameter (a model). `~publish("topic", value)` sends one. The Redis cache: `~cacheGet(key)`, `~cacheSet(key, value, seconds = 60)`.
Its file: `components/{component}/events/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).
The smallest file of the kind (what `dragonfly make listener books Book` writes):
// What Book does with the events it receives.

rows.title: `model` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: A model: what the API reads and answers, validated.
body: A **model**: what the API reads and answers, validated.

What the API reads and answers (in `domain/models/` by folder). The rule decorators check it: `@required`, `@minLength(n)`, `@maxLength(n)`, `@min(n)`, `@max(n)`, `@pattern(r"...")`, `@email`, `@url`. An invalid body is a 422.
Its file: `components/{component}/domain/models/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).
The smallest file of the kind (what `dragonfly make model books Book` writes):

rows.title: `repository` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: The data of one entity: CRUD without writing it and queries built line by line.
body: The **data of one entity**: CRUD without writing it and queries built line by line.

The data of one entity: `NameRepository` works on `Name` (or `@repository(Entity)`). It brings `find(id)` (`Ok(entity)` / `Err(NotFound)`), `findAll()`, `save(entity)` and `remove(id)`. Each method's lines build ONE query, created for that call (`q`): `where({...})` (equality, or `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `ne`, `like`, `ilike`, `oneOf`, `isNull`, `between`), `orderBy(field, desc = true)`, `limit(n)`, `offset(n)`, `relations("tasks", "tasks.tags")` (the relations to load); the last line runs it: `getOne()` (`Result`), `getMany()`, `paginate(page, size)` (`Page<T>`: `items`, `page`, `size`, `total`, `pages`), `count()`, `exists()`, `update({...})`, `delete()`. The caller awaits it: `~characters.byName(name)`.

Another API instead of the database (ADR-0103): `@repository(path = "character")` and methods without a body with `@get(path = ":id")`, `@post`, `@put`, `@patch` or `@delete`; they call the `Http(baseUrl)` connection, `:id` takes the parameter `id`, the rest goes to the query (GET) or the body, an error status is the `Err`.
Its file: `components/{component}/data/repositories/{file}.nuc` (`{component}`: the component's folder, `{file}`: the name in snake_case).
The smallest file of the kind (what `dragonfly make repository books Book` writes):

rows.title: `tools` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: Tools for a model: each public method with a doc comment is a tool the model can call.
body: **Tools** for a model: each public method with a doc comment is a tool the model can call.

Each public method with a doc comment is a tool, and the doc comment is the description the model reads; a method without one is a helper of the others (never offered to the model). A tool can use the component's repositories.

rows.title: `usecase` — a kind of the backend platform
rows.summary: One business operation: a single method `exec` that returns a `Result`.
body: One **business operation**: a single method `exec` that returns a `Result`.

One business operation: its dependencies are injected by type; `exec` returns `Result<E, T>`. `Error` is `AppError`; the runtime has `NotFound` (404), `Invalid` (400), `Unauthorized` (401), `Forbidden` (403) and `Conflict` (409).

rows.title: The backend platform of Dragonfly
rows.summary: The backend platform: HTTP APIs, data, events and AI agents. 16 kinds, 34 decorators, 11 plugins; built by the dialects fastapi, nestjs (default: fastapi).
body: A project of the platform is written once in Nuclear and builds with any of its dialects (`fastapi`, `nestjs`; `fastapi` when none is named). Create one: `dragonfly new <name> -p backend`.
- `appConfig`: The configuration of the app: its connections (databases, Redis, Kafka, models, vectors).
- `config`: The configuration of one component: connections only it uses.
- `entity`: A table of the project's database.
- `repository`: The data of one entity: CRUD without writing it and queries built line by line.
- `model`: A model: what the API reads and answers, validated.
- `usecase`: One business operation: a single method `exec` that returns a `Result`.
- `appcomponent`: The facade of a component: aliases to its use cases.
- `service`: Helpers of the use cases: mappings, transformations, calculations without state.
- `aggregate`: Business rules several use cases share (a cart with its totals).
- `listener`: A Kafka consumer: `@consumer("topic")` methods receive the messages.
- `tools`: Tools for a model: each public method with a doc comment is a tool the model can call.
- `agent`: An agent: a model with tools and a system prompt, with memory per thread.
- `graph`: A graph of steps: its methods are the nodes.
